propositions: The generic reads-under-sync-contention property does not subsume the original show regression test because it misses partial-success faults (empty-shape payloads and incomplete records) caught only by the original oracle
Fault seeds F3 (empty JSON object) and F6 (missing ticket_id field) are detected by test_cli_show_complete_or_erroring_under_write_burst but missed by both generic tests, establishing non-subsumption

The original burst test does not detect the slim-fetch-ledge regression it is named for (F1 timeout reversion only caught by held-lock tests), matching Go's precedent of deleting unreliable storm tests rather than deterministic ones
Both test files must be retained as complements because the generic property catches faults (F5/F7) missed by the original, creating bidirectional non-subsumption
Consolidation would forfeit detection of the F3/F6 partial-success class and provides zero runner savings, contradicting the overlapping-runtime hypothesis from triage
